business_summary: Visa runs the world's largest electronic payments network (VisaNet). It does NOT lend money or issue cards; banks issue Visa-branded cards and Visa carries the authorization, clearing and settlement messages between the shopper's bank and the merchant's bank. It earns a fee per transaction (data processing revenue), a fee on dollar volume (service revenue), a higher-margin fee on cross-border payments (international transaction revenue), and a fast-growing 'other revenue' line from value-added services, all partly offset by incentives paid to banks and other clients. In fiscal 2026 (year ended 2026-09-30) Visa processed 281.3 billion transactions (+9%) and earned $45.9B of net revenue (+15%) at a ~61% GAAP operating margin. There is almost no extra cost per transaction. Revenue compounds with global consumer spending and the long shift from cash and checks to digital payments.

moat.type: Network effect + global scale + brand trust + high switching costs; near-duopoly with Mastercard (the two control roughly 77% of the US credit-card market)

quality.revenue_growth_3y: 12.0% CAGR (FY2023 net revenue $32.653B -> FY2026 $45.903B). FY2026 alone +15%; quarterly growth decelerated through the year: Q1 +15%, Q2 +17%, Q3 +14%, Q4 +13%. Management guides FY2027 adjusted net revenue growth to 'low double digits' with Q2 FY2027 the low point
quality.gross_margin: n/a for a network business. FY2026 GAAP operating margin 61.2% ($28.110B operating income / $45.903B net revenue). Q4 FY2026 was 59.8% ($7.262B / $12.139B). Client incentives (a deduction from gross revenue) grew 21% in Q4 and 16% for the year, faster than net revenue (+13% and +15%)
quality.roic: ~40% (FY2026 NOPAT ~$23.5B = $28.110B operating income x (1 - 16.3% effective tax rate, $4.589B tax / $28.093B pretax), on invested capital ~$58.2B = total equity $36.111B + total debt $22.071B at 2026-09-30)
quality.net_debt_to_ebitda: ~0.27x (total debt $22.071B = $19.355B long-term + $2.716B current maturities, minus cash and equivalents plus investment securities $14.177B = ~$7.9B net debt; FY2026 EBITDA ~$29.5B = $28.110B operating income + $1.403B D&A)
quality.fcf_positive: yes - FY2026 free cash flow ~$22.06B ($23.728B operating cash flow minus $1.671B capex); FCF per share ~$11.57 on 1,907M FY2026 diluted weighted-average class A (as-converted) shares

valuation.method: Average of two methods via code/valuation.py. (1) P/E: FY2026 GAAP diluted EPS $12.32 x 24/28/32 = $296/$345/$394. (2) FCF yield: FY2026 FCF per share $11.57 at 5.2%/4.3%/3.6% = $223/$269/$321. WHAT CHANGED vs the 2026-09-17 thesis (base $291.73 -> $307.01, +5.2%): ONLY the earnings and cash-flow inputs moved, because the full fiscal year is now reported (GAAP EPS $11.76 TTM -> $12.32 FY2026; FCF/share $10.93 -> $11.57). The multiples and required yields are deliberately UNCHANGED: the Fed's last move was a hike to 3.75-4.00% (2026-09-16) and the October FOMC decision is due at 2:00 PM ET on 2026-10-28, after this refresh, so there is no new reason to change the discount assumptions. CROSS-CHECK: on FY2026 NON-GAAP EPS $13.27 the same multiples give $318/$372/$425, so even on adjusted earnings the stock is slightly above base value (MoS -8%). Sell-side targets updated after the Q4 report cluster at $425-$480 (aggregator-sourced, not used in the band). At $401.30 the stock is ~31% ABOVE our GAAP base fair value and above the top of the band: V IS OVERVALUED ON OUR FRAMEWORK AND IS NOT A BUY TODAY.

bull_case: Wide-moat near-duopoly: VisaNet's global web of issuers, merchants and acquirers is effectively impossible to replicate, and the People's Bank of China has now approved Visa to begin preparing for domestic processing in mainland China, a new long-term market.

Record year: FY2026 net revenue $45.9B (+15%), GAAP EPS $12.32 (+21%), non-GAAP EPS $13.27 (+16%), with payments volume +9% and cross-border volume +13% in constant dollars and processed transactions +9% to 281.3B.
Exceptional economics: 61.2% FY2026 GAAP operating margin, ~40% ROIC, capex of only $1.67B on $45.9B of revenue, and ~$22.1B of free cash flow.
Value-added services are scaling fast: 'other revenue' grew 40% to $5.7B in FY2026 and data processing revenue grew 17%, reducing dependence on pure swipe economics.

Fortress balance sheet (net debt ~0.27x EBITDA) and heavy capital return: $20.5B of buybacks and $5.1B of dividends in FY2026, $24.4B of repurchase authorisation left at 2026-09-30, and the quarterly dividend raised 16% to $0.780.

Visa is positioning itself inside the stablecoin and agentic-commerce shift rather than being bypassed by it. Management cites a stablecoin settlement run rate above $25B annualised and nearly 50 AI partners live on Visa Intelligent Commerce, but describes agentic commerce as 'still very early' (call commentary, aggregator-sourced).
The largest US legal overhang is resolved on known terms: the ~$38B merchant interchange settlement was court-approved on 2026-06-09.
risks: VALUATION IS THE PRIMARY RISK. At $401.30 the stock is ~31% above our GAAP base fair value of $307.01 and above the top of our band ($357.81). It trades at 32.6x FY2026 GAAP EPS ($12.32) and 30.2x non-GAAP EPS ($13.27), and yields only ~0.78% ($0.780 quarterly). The price rose ~8.6% since the last refresh while our fair value rose ~5.2%, so the gap WIDENED. A 12% margin of safety implies a buy price of roughly $270; under the cautious 18% rule it is roughly $252.

Growth is slowing. Quarterly net revenue growth went 17% -> 14% -> 13% over the last three quarters, and management guides FY2027 to low-double-digit revenue growth and low-double-digit-to-low-teens adjusted EPS growth, with the tax rate rising to ~19% from ~16% in FY2026. Paying ~32x GAAP earnings for ~11-13% growth leaves little room for disappointment.

Client incentives are outgrowing revenue: +18% in Q3 and +21% in Q4 FY2026 against net revenue +14% and +13%. The CFO said to expect 'a higher volume of incentives in '27' because ~25% of payments volume is up for renewal (vs ~20% in 2026). This is a direct squeeze on the take rate, and our incentives sell trigger is now 2 of the 4 consecutive quarters needed to fire.
Rising rates work against long-duration compounders. The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, and a further hike would pressure the multiple.

Reported GAAP earnings stay noisy: FY2026 included a $1.7B litigation provision, $563M of severance and a $282M Visa Foundation donation, partly offset by a $314M deferred tax benefit. Litigation provisions now recur every year.

Regulatory: the Credit Card Competition Act (mandated alternative routing) is still pending. It failed to be attached to the Senate housing bill in March 2026, but it has a presidential endorsement and new cosponsors. The approved MDL settlement also lets merchants decline premium cards and surcharge.
Disruption: account-to-account and real-time rails (FedNow, UPI, Pix), stablecoins and Big Tech wallets could route volume around card networks over time; the outcome is uncertain.

Cyclicality and geopolitics: high-margin cross-border volume falls in recessions, and management cites the CEMEA conflict and FX volatility as drags in FY2027 guidance. International transaction revenue grew only 8% in FY2026, well below the group's 15%.
what_would_break_thesis: GAAP operating margin falls below 55% for two consecutive fiscal quarters (it was 59.8% in Q4 FY2026 and 61.2% for FY2026).
Net revenue shrinks year-over-year for two consecutive quarters outside a clearly identified macro recession.

Client incentives grow faster than net revenue for four consecutive quarters (STATUS: 2 of 4 - Q3 FY2026 +18% vs +14%, Q4 FY2026 +21% vs +13%. If Q1 and Q2 FY2027 also show incentives outgrowing net revenue, this trigger fires).
Free cash flow turns negative for a full fiscal year, or annual/TTM free cash flow falls more than 25% below the prior year's absent a one-off (FY2026 ~$22.1B).

A regulatory ruling, statute (e.g. passage of the Credit Card Competition Act) or settlement that structurally caps network fees or mandates alternative routing in a major market and is expected to cut Visa's net revenue by more than ~15%.
Cross-border volume growth stalls structurally (negative or near-zero constant-dollar growth for four consecutive quarters outside a recession); FY2026 total cross-border was +13%.
Processed transaction growth falls below 3% YoY for two consecutive quarters while global consumer spending is still growing (Q4 FY2026: +10%).
A serious accounting red flag, restatement, or a material weakness disclosed in internal controls.
catalysts: Q1 FY2027 earnings (expected late January 2027): the key test of the client-incentive trigger (2 of 4 quarters so far) and of management's guide for low-double-digit revenue growth, roughly 1 point below Q4's growth rate.
FOMC decision on 2026-10-28 (after this refresh): another hike would argue for lower multiples, while a hold leaves the band unchanged.

A broad market pullback: our buy zone (~$270 at a 12% margin of safety, ~$252 under the cautious 18% rule) needs a ~33-37% decline, so fair value must also grow into the price. At ~11-13% EPS growth that takes roughly 2-3 years with no price change.
Continued buybacks ($24.4B authorised remaining) shrinking the share count.
Implementation of the MDL settlement (premium-card declines and surcharging) and any movement on the Credit Card Competition Act.
China domestic processing preparations and growth of value-added services (other revenue +40% in FY2026).
